question: After independently choosing the mechanically supported 90-degree orientation and registering one rotated scan back to plate coordinates, does the unchanged P6AT cross-spectral coherence discriminator identify same-plate structure over wrong-region and shifted controls?

primary_sources.title: SCORPION: A Multi-Scanner Whole-Slide Image Dataset for Cross-Scanner Analysis
primary_sources.role: latest frozen cross-scanner coherence method parent

primary_sources.title: Precise Photometric Measurements from a 1903 Photographic Plate Using a Commercial Scanner
primary_sources.role: same-plate perpendicular-scan experiment and scanner-axis nuisance evidence

rotated.description: same 2.4 by 2.4 inch central area at focus +1.4, plate rotated by 90 degrees

registration.input: uint16 grayscale upper-eight-bits, area-resized to maximum side 1024
registration.orientation_selection: maximum SIFT-RANSAC inlier count, then inlier fraction, then +90 tie break; coherence and control scores forbidden

analysis.wrong_region_control: cyclic next patch in row-major order from rotated scan

forbidden: modify or rescue the completed P6L source/correlation decision
use f0007 or f0008 pixels or select a crop from their results
choose orientation, registration, patches, frequencies or thresholds from coherence outcomes
interpret shared structure as isolated emulsion grain or scanner-independent NPS
fit a film profile, scanner profile, colour operator or product default
claim_ceiling: one CC-BY-4.0 1903 glass photographic plate scanned twice at perpendicular orientations on one Epson 12000XL workflow; generic same-material shared-structure method evidence only, not isolated emulsion NPS, scanner calibration, modern stock transfer or product evidence.
